strategy_title: Autotune Larger XBLOCK/num_warps Causes Regression via Register Pressure
strategy_description: Adding @triton.autotune with larger XBLOCK (512–2048) and higher num_warps (4–16) increased registers per thread from 18 to 32, which reduced L1 cache hit rate from 84.9% to 74.5% and nearly doubled executed instructions (5.1M → 9.4M). Although achieved occupancy improved (60.8% → 84.1%) and eligible warps per scheduler rose (1.95 → 6.64), the increased instruction count and register spill pressure caused warp cycles per issued instruction to worsen (13.87 → 16.08 cycles), resulting in a 38% longer kernel duration. When a kernel is already register-efficient (≤18 regs/thread) and has high L1 hit rates for broadcast/parameter loads, enlarging XBLOCK forces the compiler to allocate more registers, degrading cache utilization and negating the latency-hiding benefit of more warps.
slow_pseudocode:
@triton.autotune(
    configs=[
        triton.Config({'XBLOCK': 512},  num_warps=4),
        triton.Config({'XBLOCK': 512},  num_warps=8),
        triton.Config({'XBLOCK': 1024}, num_warps=4),
        triton.Config({'XBLOCK': 1024}, num_warps=8),
        triton.Config({'XBLOCK': 2048}, num_warps=8),
        triton.Config({'XBLOCK': 2048}, num_warps=16),
    ],
    key=['xnumel'],
)
@triton.jit
def kernel(in_out_ptr0, ..., xnumel, XBLOCK: tl.constexpr):
    # kernel body unchanged
    ...
grid = (triton.cdiv(xnumel, 128),)
kernel[grid](arg_0, ..., 1881600)  # XBLOCK chosen by autotune
applicable_when: Never apply this specific strategy when the baseline kernel already uses a small XBLOCK (≤128) with low register count (≤18 regs/thread) and high L1 hit rate (>80%) for broadcast parameter loads. The CPIStall signal alone is insufficient justification if eligible warps are already >1.5 and L1 hit rate is high.
do_not_apply_when: Kernel has ≤18 registers/thread and L1/TEX hit rate >80%; increasing XBLOCK will cause the compiler to allocate more registers (observed jump to 32), reducing L1 residency for cached broadcast tensors and increasing total instruction count, causing net regression despite improved occupancy.
framework_notes: In Triton, larger XBLOCK values cause the compiler to allocate more registers to hold the wider vector of intermediate values, which can unexpectedly increase register pressure. The autotune grid was also left as a fixed (triton.cdiv(xnumel, 128),) rather than a lambda using meta['XBLOCK'], meaning all configs ran with the same grid size regardless of XBLOCK — this is an implementation flaw that would cause incorrect tiling for XBLOCK != 128.
